Public Environmental Education and Climate Campaigns
Ministerial Citizen Complaints & Petition Redress Desk

faqs.question: What is the primary role of the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources?
faqs.answer: The Ministry formulates and oversees Lagos State's policies on environmental sanitation, climate adaptation, stormwater drainage infrastructure, flood prevention, and water resources management, coordinating all affiliated environmental agencies.

faqs.question: Who is the Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources?
faqs.answer: The Honourable Commissioner is Mr. Tokunbo Philip Wahab, an accomplished lawyer and alumnus of the Harvard Kennedy School and Harvard Business School.

faqs.question: Where can I submit a general environmental complaint or petition?
faqs.answer: You can lodge complaints directly through the Ministry's Citizen Complaints Desk on https://moelagos.gov.ng, or call the Rapid Response lines on 0810 255 3775 or 0802 232 0497.

agencies.name: Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency
agencies.mandate: Primary regulatory science and environmental enforcement body tasked with pollution control, noise regulation, industrial effluents, air quality monitoring, and hazardous chemical management.
agencies.address: LASEPA Complex, Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja, Lagos State
services: Noise Permits for Concerts & Public Events

faqs.question: Which agency handles noise pollution complaints in Lagos State?
faqs.answer: Noise pollution complaints are strictly handled by the Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency (LASEPA). Official contact: 0811 188 8885, 0901 055 5557 or via https://lasepa.gov.ng.

faqs.question: What are the legal noise limits in Lagos State?
faqs.answer: Under LASEPA regulations, allowable limits are: Residential: 55 decibels (Day), 45 decibels (Night); Commercial: 65 decibels (Day), 60 decibels (Night). Night limits take effect at 10:00 PM.

faqs.question: How do I report a noisy club, church, or factory?
faqs.answer: Report directly to LASEPA via https://lasepa.gov.ng or call 0811 188 8885. Environmental surveillance officers inspect the location with sound level meters and issue enforcement notices.

agencies.name: Lagos Waste Management Authority
agencies.mandate: Regulatory and administrative oversight of municipal, commercial, industrial, and medical waste management, coordinating private sector participation (PSP) waste collectors across all local councils.
agencies.address: 3, Otto Road, Ijora Oloye, Lagos State

faqs.question: How do I arrange household waste collection in Lagos?
faqs.answer: Household waste collection in Lagos is carried out by private PSP operators licensed and assigned to specific streets by LAWMA. Residents must register with their designated PSP operator and place bagged refuse in standard bins.

faqs.question: Does LAWMA collect every house's trash directly?
faqs.answer: No. LAWMA is the waste-sector regulator and coordinator. Domestic refuse is collected by licensed private PSP operators assigned to each ward. LAWMA intervenes on expressways, markets, and in cases of PSP failure.

faqs.question: Is patronizing cart pushers legal in Lagos?
faqs.answer: No. Cart pushing is illegal under Lagos State environmental laws because cart pushers routinely dump waste into drainage canals. Both the cart pusher and the resident who engages them face legal penalties.

agencies.name: Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency
agencies.officialName: Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency
agencies.mandate: Administration, greening, beautification, landscaping, and maintenance of public recreational parks, gardens, open spaces, and statutory tree conservation across Lagos State.
agencies.address: Plot 1, Commercial Scheme, Beside Elephant Cement House, CBD, Alausa, Ikeja
services: Public Recreational Park Booking & Event Permits
Annual Lagos Tree Planting Day Coordination

faqs.question: How can I book a Lagos State public park for an event?
faqs.answer: Public parks such as JJT Park (Alausa) or Ndubuisi Kanu Park can be booked online via the official LASPARK portal at https://lasparkportal.lagosstate.gov.ng or at LASPARK headquarters.

faqs.question: Can I cut down a tree in my compound without government approval?
faqs.answer: No. It is a statutory violation in Lagos State to fell or severely prune a mature tree without an official Tree Permit issued by LASPARK, regardless of whether the tree is on private property.

faqs.question: How do I apply for a Tree Felling or Pruning Permit?
faqs.answer: Apply through https://lasparkportal.lagosstate.gov.ng. LASPARK arborists inspect the tree for structural hazards and issue official clearance with compensatory planting guidelines.

agencies.name: Lagos Water Corporation
agencies.mandate: Production, scientific purification, transmission, and retail distribution of piped potable drinking water to homes, businesses, and industries across Lagos State.
services: New Residential & Commercial Piped Water Connections
Operation of Adiyan, Iju, and Ishasi Waterworks

faqs.question: How can I apply for a new municipal water connection in Lagos?
faqs.answer: Applications for piped municipal water connections are submitted to the Lagos Water Corporation (LWC) at https://lagoswater.org or through the nearest LWC regional area office.

faqs.question: What is the difference between LWC and LSWRC?
faqs.answer: LWC is the public utility operator that produces, purifies, and pipes tap water. LSWRC is the independent commission that regulates the water sector, tariffs, and private borehole drillers.

faqs.question: How do I report a burst water main in my street?
faqs.answer: Report public pipe bursts to LWC customer lines on 0704 597 3000 or 0704 597 3001 for rapid dispatch of maintenance engineers.

agencies.name: Lagos State Water Regulatory Commission
agencies.mandate: Independent economic and technical regulation of water supply, wastewater services, commercial groundwater extraction, borehole drilling contractors, and packaged drinking water safety.
agencies.address: 1st Floor, Block 16, Lagos State Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja

faqs.question: Do I need a permit from LSWRC to drill a commercial borehole?
faqs.answer: Yes. All commercial and industrial boreholes, as well as borehole drilling contractors in Lagos State, must be registered and licensed by LSWRC to prevent aquifer contamination and land subsidence.

faqs.question: Which agency monitors the safety of sachet and bottled drinking water in Lagos?
faqs.answer: The Lagos State Water Regulatory Commission (LSWRC) conducts periodic chemical and microbiological surveillance on packaged drinking water factories across Lagos.

faqs.question: What is the difference between LSWRC and LWC?
faqs.answer: LWC (Lagos Water Corporation) is the public municipal water utility that produces, purifies, and pipes tap water to homes. LSWRC (Lagos State Water Regulatory Commission) is the independent commission that regulates the entire water sector, licenses commercial borehole drillers, and monitors packaged water safety.

agencies.name: Lagos State Wastewater Management Office
agencies.mandate: Regulation, collection, transportation, and scientific treatment of municipal sewage, septage, fecal sludge, and domestic wastewater, certifying decentralized wastewater systems.
agencies.address: Ministry of the Environment Complex, Block 16, Alausa, Ikeja
services: Public Wastewater Treatment Plants (Odo Iya Alaro, Abule Egba)
Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Plant (DEWATS) Certification for Estates

faqs.question: Which agency handles wastewater and sewage in Lagos State?
faqs.answer: The Lagos State Wastewater Management Office (LSWMO) handles sewage, septage, and domestic wastewater systems. Official website: https://lswmo.lg.gov.ng.

faqs.question: Are residential estates required to install wastewater treatment plants?
faqs.answer: Yes. Residential estates and commercial facilities with 25 or more units are mandated by LSWMO to install Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Plants (DEWATS) before discharging effluent.

faqs.question: Who handles domestic sewage soakaways versus street rainwater gutters?
faqs.answer: Domestic sewage, septic soakaways, and fecal sludge are managed and regulated by LSWMO, whereas street rainwater gutters, collector drains, and stormwater canals are managed by the Office of Drainage Services and Water Resources (ODSWR).

agencies.name: Lagos State Signage and Advertisement Agency
agencies.officialName: Lagos State Signage and Advertisement Agency
agencies.mandate: Statutory regulation, control, and permitting of all outdoor advertising displays, billboards, signboards, mobile vehicle branding, street furniture, and temporary event banners in Lagos State.
agencies.address: Plot 4, Commercial Scheme, Alausa, Ikeja, Lagos State
services: Removal of Illegal or Hazardous Outdoor Advertising Structures

faqs.question: How can I obtain an outdoor advertising permit in Lagos State?
faqs.answer: Applications for outdoor billboards, signboards, and commercial signage must be submitted to LASAA via https://lasaa.lg.gov.ng or at LASAA headquarters in Alausa.

faqs.question: Do I need a LASAA permit to brand a company delivery vehicle?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under the LASAA Law, branding on commercial vehicles, company cars, delivery vans, and logistics fleets requires a Mobile Branding Permit from LASAA.

agencies.name: Lagos Environmental Sanitation Corps
agencies.officialName: Lagos Environmental Sanitation Corps (popularly known as KAI)
agencies.mandate: Uniformed environmental law-enforcement corps established to preserve public sanitation, compel pedestrian bridge usage, eliminate illegal street trading on highway corridors, and curb open defecation.
agencies.address: Safety Arena Complex, Bolade, Oshodi, Lagos State
services: Removal of Illegal Traders from Road Setbacks and Medians
Dismantling of Unlawful Shanties on Drainage Alignments
Prosecution of Sanitation Offenders in Environmental Mobile Courts

faqs.question: What is the official name of the KAI agency?
faqs.answer: The official statutory name is the Lagos Environmental Sanitation Corps (LAGESC), popularly referred to by its operational moniker KAI (Kick Against Indiscipline).

faqs.question: Is crossing the expressway instead of using a pedestrian bridge an offense in Lagos?
faqs.answer: Yes. Crossing expressways where pedestrian bridges are provided is a punishable offense enforced by LAGESC (KAI) officers. Offenders are arraigned before the Special Environmental Mobile Court.

agencies.name: Office of Drainage Services and Water Resources
agencies.officialName: Office of Drainage Services and Water Resources (MOE&WR)
agencies.mandate: Engineering design, ongoing desilting, dredging, widening, and maintenance of all primary stormwater canals, collector drains, and drainage right-of-way (RoW) enforcement across Lagos State.
agencies.address: Block 16, Lagos State Government Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja
services: Demolition of Illegal Structures Obstructing Stormwater Runoff
Seasonal High-Tide and Rainfall Flood Advisories

faqs.question: How can I report blocked drainage or community flooding in Lagos?
faqs.answer: Report blocked drainage or flooding to the Office of Drainage Services and Water Resources (ODSWR) via the Ministry Complaints Desk at https://moelagos.gov.ng or call 0810 255 3775 / 0802 344 5821.

faqs.question: Which agency clears large stormwater canals in Lagos State?
faqs.answer: The Office of Drainage Services and Water Resources (ODSWR), through its Emergency Flood Abatement Gang (EFAG), conducts the continuous desilting and dredging of primary canals. This is distinct from LAWMA's refuse collection remit.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for building over a drainage channel in Lagos?
faqs.answer: Building over a drainage channel or inside its statutory right-of-way is illegal. ODSWR serves contravention notices, marks the structure for removal, and carries out demolition without compensation to protect public safety.
